_about: Provenance for the hardware-derived constants that cross a session or
project boundary. WHY THIS EXISTS: on 2026-09-11 a correct attack law was
replaced by one 1.8x wrong, and the cause was not arithmetic -- it was a
method attributed to the wrong section. Three provenance errors happened
in one day; in every one the VALUE travelled correctly and where it came
from did not, because the value lives in the code and the provenance lived
in a comment above it. Peers quote the value.
The two fields that would have prevented that day are `convention` and
`subject`. A constant that says 'time to full level' cannot be silently
compared against a -3 dB reading, and a subject field makes 'one was a
synthesized sine and the other a resident sample' visible without reading
two sections.
`tests/test_calibration_provenance.py` asserts every `value` here against
the live constant, so a constant cannot be changed without this file
failing. That is the point: the failure is what forces the provenance to
be updated with the number.
`provenance_gap: true` marks an entry whose method or subject nobody has
written down. It is a to-do, not a defect in the value -- but a constant
with no recorded convention is one misreading away from 2026-09-11.
`detector` records HOW the quantity was read, and whether the reading was
adequate for the subject. Added 2026-09-14 after the day's single largest
source of error turned out to be detector adequacy rather than any value:
an envelope detector's window must span a fixed number of CARRIER CYCLES,
not a fixed number of milliseconds. Below about one cycle the carrier leaks
into the envelope and its peaks cross a -3 dB threshold with no attack in
progress -- 0.052 cycles gives 20.6 dB of swing on a tone with no
modulation at all, 5.2 cycles gives 0.26 dB (eosed §121). A constant read
through an under-resolved detector is wrong in a way its own residuals
cannot show, so the field says `null` where nobody recorded the method
rather than being left out.

entries.name: _AK_ATTAK1_TIME
entries.quantity: ATTAK1 byte -> seconds, t = a * exp(b * byte)
entries.convention: time to FULL level (the ramp is linear in amplitude)
entries.method: Hilbert envelope, line/plateau knee, 7 rungs, residuals -1.4%..+2.1%
entries.subject: synthesized CONSTANT-AMPLITUDE sine, 33 Hz, SUSTN1 99, probe note 24, velocity 80
entries.known_limits: CONFIRMED BY THREE INDEPENDENT MEASUREMENTS AGREEING TO ~1%. §141 (2026-08-20, a different session, method and rig -- time to 90% of the plateau on a resident sine) agrees within 2% at ATTAK1 80, 90 and 99. §234 (2026-09-13, measure.py + Hilbert knee) is the fit itself. A third capture on 2026-09-14, after two analysis bugs in that day's newer path were found and fixed, reads 0.1418 / 3.5234 / 9.6018 at rungs 60 / 90 / 99 against the law's 0.1410 / 3.5520 / 9.6290 -- +0.55%, -0.80%, -0.28%. THE FAST-END TERM AND THE PROGRAM-DEPENDENCE ARE BOTH WITHDRAWN, and both came from the same constant: JACK runs at 48000 and the newer analysis scripts had SR = 44100 hardcoded, which scaled every time by 8.8% AND opened the analysis window at int(0.4 * 44100) = 0.3675 s, i.e. 32.5 ms before the note. The offset is 23% of an ATTAK1 60 attack and 0.3% of a 99, which is why the discrepancy fitted neither a constant nor a factor: it was both at once (s3ked §239, §240). measure.py writes WAVs and takes the rate from the file, which is why the older path -- the one this law rests on -- could not make either mistake. REMAINING LIMITS: fitted 60..99, so below 60 is extrapolated and unmeasured; and repeatability is rung-dependent by a factor of a hundred, +-5% at ATTAK1 60 against 0.03-0.04% at 90 and 99, because short attacks contain few envelope steps. Quote the rung with the figure. A residual detector floor of ~11 ms exists at ATTAK1 0, note-independent and flat to ~2 ms across a hundredfold sweep of detector width in two detector families, so it is real and much smaller than the 47 ms first reported.
entries.supersedes: (0.00015, 0.10545) 2026-09-11, which was read at -3 dB through a 5 ms RMS window on a 33 Hz tone -- 1.41 x 1.26 = 1.78x slow
withdrawn_caveats: §236's program-dependence (the same byte giving a 33% different attack on a second program) was WITHDRAWN by §237 the same day: it compared one capture path against another, with the program riding along, because the same program had never been measured twice. Nine variables had been correctly eliminated from a comparison with no effect in it.

'The law may be out by up to 28%' stood in this field for 20 minutes and was wrong twice over -- the disagreement was rung-dependent, and the +-5% repeatability it leaned on is specific to ATTAK1 60. Both figures had travelled here without their conditions.
'9% at 80-99 and 34% at 60, fast end unverified' was the third version, and is superseded by §239/§240 finding both bugs in the newer analysis path. There is one path; it was mis-analysed.

THIS FIELD WAS REWRITTEN FIVE TIMES ON 2026-09-14, each time honestly and each superseded within the hour. Kept visible rather than tidied: the point of this file was never to be right first time, it was to make a correction land in one obvious place instead of in a comment nobody re-reads.
entries.detector: Hilbert envelope, line/plateau knee. IMMUNE BY CONSTRUCTION: the Hilbert envelope is exact for a single tone and has no window to choose. This matters here -- the subject's 33 Hz carrier is 0.165 cycles in a 5 ms window, about 11 dB of swing, and the 5 ms RMS reading of this same capture ran 17-33% SHORT of the Hilbert one. That reading is what the 2026-09-11 regression was fitted to.

entries.name: _AK_RELSE1_RATE
entries.convention: a RATE over a span, not a duration
entries.known_limits: Fitted 45..99 only. Below 35 the fit collapses to r2 0.51-0.73 AND stops depending on the setting, which is the signature of measuring the rig's own tail rather than the envelope. Marked unmeasurable rather than filled in.
entries.detector: log-space fit to a dB/s slope; window and subject carrier not recorded. Below RELSE1 35 the fit collapses and stops depending on the setting, which is the signature of measuring the rig's tail rather than the field.

entries.name: _AK_DECAY1_RATE
entries.convention: a RATE over a span, not a duration

entries.name: AKAI_FILTER_LAW
entries.quantity: FILFRQ byte -> Hz, Hz = a * exp(b * byte)
entries.convention: the -3 dB corner, which is what every source format means by cutoff
entries.method: direct measurement of the -3 dB point
entries.known_limits: §54 claims the same quantity by another route (peak sits AT the corner, does not move with FILQ) and disagrees by 1.29x. That is an unexplained disagreement, not a definitional offset, and s3ked has it open with one sweep intended to yield both numbers. §139 is used because it measures the -3 dB point directly.
entries.detector: direct -3 dB point measurement; window and subject carrier not recorded.

entries.name: _E4XT_ATK_SLOWDOWN
entries.quantity: multiplier applied to a requested attack before encoding
entries.convention: 1.0 means the writer targets the machine's -3 dB point, NOT its full traversal
entries.method: a CHOICE, not a measurement -- which point of a convex curve to match
entries.known_limits: THE RECORDED REASON IN THE SOURCE IS STILL WRONG AND IS SCHEDULED FOR REWRITE. It claims the machine agrees with `intends` 'at the same convention'; those are two conventions. Matching at full traversal instead would need ~1.17 -- as measured on ONE preset, spread across presets unmeasured. 1.4125 is a property of a LINEAR ramp and must not be carried here: the E4XT's is strongly convex, 28% delivered at its own nominal attack time (§ATTACKSHAPE).
entries.detector: not a detector reading at all -- a choice of which point of a convex curve to match. The measurements it is weighed against were read at a fixed 5 ms window on transposed material, which eosed §121 shows can manufacture a note-effect of 1.25x where none exists.

entries.name: ENV_RATE_SWEEP_A
entries.method: extrapolated from a fit over bytes 60..100
entries.known_limits: EXTRAPOLATED, not measured, at byte 0 itself. The cross-check that supported this ladder read byte 89 as 10.1 s on one preset and 9.10 s on another -- an 11% disagreement recorded as agreement, corrected 2026-09-14 to 'the byte is the MAIN term, not the only term'. Neither cross-check row recorded its note or its preset. THE EXPLANATION PREVIOUSLY OFFERED HERE IS WITHDRAWN: this field said the 11% might be the E4XT's 'measured note-dependence of 1.25x across 55 semitones'. eosed §121 (2026-09-14) shows there IS no note-dependence -- the 1.25x was a fixed 5 ms detector on TRANSPOSED material. A note ladder plays one sample at many rates, so the material's own modulation stretches by 2^((origkey-note)/12) and a fixed window resolves a different number of sample-periods at every rung. Scale the detector with the playback rate and the effect goes flat (t90 ratio 0.962). The control that settles it: a preset with an INSTANT attack still read 0.060 s at note 16 against 0.020 s at note 64 -- a 3x note-effect on a rise that does not exist. So the 11% is unexplained again, and the paths it was blamed on are both cleared. Smoothing can CREATE a spread it cannot remove: the widest rate-scaled window here is 31.7 ms against a 2.570 s measurement, 1.24%, which cannot hide a 1.7 s effect but can manufacture one out of a 30 dB ripple crossing a threshold early.
entries.detector: fixed 5 ms window. EXPOSED: the ladder rows record neither preset, note nor carrier, so cycles-per-window cannot be reconstructed for any row. The 11% cross-check gap is unexplained and this is one reason it cannot be chased.

entries.name: ENV_RATE_SWEEP_K
entries.quantity: natural-log step per rate byte, dB/s law
entries.known_limits:
DISAGREES WITH ENV_RATE_K (0.0581) BY 2.8%, which is inside the noise of both fits, and nothing yet picks between them. The firmware route to settling it is CLOSED: EOS 4.61 and 4.70 ship as an LZEXE stub plus a packed floppy image whose decompressor lives in the E4XT's boot ROM (eosed §116, entropy + autocorrelation + 36 schemes + an XOR whose expected agreement was computed before running). It stays with the captures. FIRMWARE READING, 2026-09-14 (eosed §122, §124): a 128-entry u16 big-endian table, descending 65535->4, one entry per MIDI parameter byte. Its log-slope over bytes 60-100 is 0.05638 (r2 0.99994) -- **0.2% from ENV_RATE_SWEEP_K's 0.0565 and 3.0% from ENV_RATE_K's 0.0581**, so if the identification holds the 2.8% disagreement between our two constants resolves in favour of 0.0565 and ENV_RATE_K is the one to move. **THE VERSION CAVEAT IS CLOSED BY DIRECT COMPARISON.** It was found in the 4.62 image while the bench runs 4.70, and every argument bridging that gap was inferential -- a structural one, a community recollection, and an absence-of-evidence reading of E-MU's 4.7 addendum that was retracted the same hour when Jan pointed out the addendum omits a real audible filter change and that 4.7 was never officially released. None of that is needed now: `eosflash` (Nkrypth/Madlabz), a public CLI for the EOS container, decompressed 4.70 (magic 0x76543211, ColdFire MCF5206E, 1.43:1, checksum verified), and **the table's 256 bytes appear VERBATIM in the decompressed 4.70 image, twice, at 0x41490 and 0x1da390.** It is a reading of the firmware the bench actually runs. **THE IDENTITY IS NO LONGER INFERRED: it was discharged by reading the CONSUMER** (eosed §125). With 4.70 decompressed and the load base at 0x20000, the table sits at 0x00061690 and is referenced exactly TWICE, both in one routine that ColdFire decodes with zero invalid words -- an envelope segment stepper. It forms an index as `(rate field + a second term) >> 5`, clamps it to 0..127, reads `table[index]` as u16, multiplies by elapsed ticks and either subtracts or adds it to the running level. **The two references are the falling and rising branches**, which is a structural prediction the reading makes and a shape match could never have made. Corroborated independently from the corpus: table[0] = 65535 is the largest increment, i.e. the fastest possible segment, and 67.1% of corpus rate bytes are byte 0 -- two unrelated sources, with the code explaining the agreement rather than sharing it. STILL NOT ACTED ON, because a firmware table says what the machine intends and our constant has to match what leaves the converters. Confirming on hardware **should be aimed at bytes 20-59, not at the fitted range**: 90.3% of on-curve corpus usage is there and the fitted range is where we already know the answer. **AND A CONSEQUENCE FOR ANY FUTURE WRITER WORK: the index is a SUM, at 32x the MIDI byte's resolution.** The stored byte is a contribution to a rate, not a rate, so envelope-rate modulation moves in steps no parameter read can see, and the clamp is applied after the addition. Whether that reaches a conversion depends on whether anything in real material modulates an envelope rate; 700,257 active modulation cords across 95,132 corpus voices use 43 distinct destination bytes, and which of those are envelope rates is with eosed. **AND THE TABLE IS NOT A SINGLE EXPONENTIAL**: slopes run 0.128 below byte 20, 0.0596 over 20-59, 0.0564 over 60-100 and 0.0778 above 100, so our law is right exactly where it was fitted. CORPUS WEIGHT, measured here over 380 banks and 285,396 amp-envelope rate bytes: 67.1% are byte 0 (the 'instant' encoding, not on the curve), and of the rest 90.3% fall in 20-59, 7.9% in the fitted 60-100, 1.7% below 20 and 0.1% above 100. Integrating the piecewise table against our single exponential, we are 4-5% out where the corpus lives (bytes 44 and 46 are the two commonest in the whole corpus) and 2x-3x out where almost nothing does. So a refit of ONE exponential would trade a 4% error over 90% of the corpus for a better fit over 8% of it; if this is ever acted on it should become piecewise. **A CLAIMED THIRD LINE OF EVIDENCE WAS RETRACTED WITHIN THREE MINUTES OF BEING WRITTEN HERE, AND THE RETRACTION IS THE USEFUL PART (2026-09-14).** The claim: a Key+ -> VEnvAtk cord at +10% shifts the index 7.94 bytes and the attack 3.020 s -> 1.940 s, implying a log-slope of 0.05574 -- so the firmware's 0.0565 predicts the ratio three times better than ENV_RATE_K's 0.0581, on a measurement neither was fitted to. **It is circular.** The 7.94 was not measured: it was derived as `index_for(T[72] * t_base / t_measured)`, log-interpolating THE FIRMWARE TABLE itself. So feeding it back through a candidate k tests only whether that k equals the table's local slope, which over bytes 64-72 is 0.05572. It restates what reading the table already said. **AND THE CIRCULARITY CHECK FAILED IN A WAY WORTH RECORDING.** The test was: a circular derivation would reproduce the ratio EXACTLY, so a 1.9% miss rules it out. Wrong -- the miss is the table's own deviation from a pure exponential over that span. **A circular derivation through a NON-EXPONENTIAL table produces an inexact-looking agreement, which is the most convincing possible disguise.** So there are two lines, not three: the table's slope over 60-100, and the corpus's byte-0/instant agreement. The cord experiment contributes the full-scale floor and the sign, and nothing about ENV_RATE_K. **WHAT WOULD BE NON-CIRCULAR, and it refines the hardware check:** a byte shift obtained without the table. Set rate byte 60 and rate byte 100, measure both times, take the ratio -- no table, no cord, no fit. **Two rungs rather than one**, because the ratio is what discriminates the constants and a single rung cannot. **SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT 2026-09-14, AND THE ANSWER IS 'DO NOT MOVE IT' (eosed §129).** Two rungs per pair, both inside one table segment, each rung measured twice, audio and byte numbers only -- the table is never touched, so this is independent of everything above:
    byte      25      55      60     100
    t90    0.210   1.160   1.500  14.520 s
    k per byte, at matched 2 ms smoothing:  60->100 = 0.05649   25->55 = 0.05866
The two bands differ by 3.8% in the direction the table predicts, so §122's PIECEWISE STRUCTURE is now established without reading the table. **Each of our two constants is right in one band and wrong in the other**: over bytes 60-100 the measurement is ~0.0564, so ENV_RATE_SWEEP_K's 0.0565 fits and ENV_RATE_K's 0.0581 is +2.9% off; over bytes 25-55 it is ~0.0587, so ENV_RATE_K fits to 1.0% and ENV_RATE_SWEEP_K is -3.8% off. **The corpus decides it: 90.3% of on-curve rate bytes sit in 20-59.** Moving ENV_RATE_K to 0.0565 would trade a good fit over 90% of the corpus for a better one over 8%. Leaving it alone is more defensible than the change the firmware table pointed at this morning; a PIECEWISE law would be better than either and is filed rather than implemented, since it would correct 2.9% on 8% of usage. LIMITS, stated: within-band spread across smoothing widths is 1.8% and 3.0% against a 3.8% between-band difference, so the DIRECTION holds at every width tried and the MAGNITUDE does not; the 25-55 slope sits 2% below the table's 0.0600; one preset, one note. **Byte 25 nearly inverted the result** -- its two takes were 0.200 and 0.220 s, exactly one 20 ms window apart on a 0.21 s rise, and at 20 ms smoothing the two bands read identical. Visible only because the rung was measured twice.

entries.name: ENV_RATE_A
entries.quantity: seconds at rate byte 0, time-alone law
entries.convention: a TIME, and only correct at the span the calibration used
entries.known_limits: Rate 0 is the deliberate 'instant' encoding and is NOT a point on this curve; `env_rate_to_seconds` must return 0 there. It used to return 0.031, and the commonest single round-trip difference over the E4B corpus was 'attack 0.0 -> 0.031' on 77.4% of zones.

entries.name: ENV_LEVELBYTE_DB_INTERCEPT
entries.quantity: dB below the attack peak at level byte 0
entries.known_limits: Named for the BYTE deliberately: `ENV_LEVEL_DB_INTERCEPT` exists for the sustain-PERCENT law and silently shadowed this one when it was first written, so every reading came out 0 dB with no error.

entries.name: KRZ_ENV_TIME_GRID
entries.quantity: K2000 envelope-time display grid, seconds per editor step; time byte = steps(seconds) + 3
entries.convention: the EDITOR's step grid, so byte 3 is 0.00 s and the finest quantum is 20 ms
entries.known_limits: The 20 ms quantum is 1/50 s and has no relation to the 41.7 ms in §KRZENVLOOP (1/24 s) -- checked 2026-09-14 and recorded as coincidence. The 27 ms release floor that trips §KRZDBLZERO is 0.5 * 20 ms / (0.2 * 1.9): this grid, _REL1_TIME_FRAC and KRZ_RELEASE_FACTOR, and nothing from the machine.
entries.detector: read off the editor's own display, not detected from audio.

entries.name: KRZ_RELEASE_FACTOR
entries.quantity: correction from the shared MPC value->seconds curve to the K2000's displayed release
entries.method: one pair: 2.63 s displayed against 1.39 s from the curve
entries.subject: AlphaPad #200
entries.known_limits: ONE OBSERVATION, ONE PROGRAM. 'roughly constant' is asserted in the source comment and is not measured across the range.
entries.detector: read off the machine's display against a curve value; one program.

entries.name: KRZ_2POLE_F0_TO_3DB
entries.convention: converts the machine's f0 label to the -3 dB corner the model carries
entries.method: confirmed four ways: gain at the corner, the -3 dB crossing, an external instrument (the MPC, measuring the same quantity), and an A/B by ear
entries.known_limits: The 4-pole is DELIBERATELY not corrected by the same route; see KRZ_4POLE_F0_TO_3DB.
entries.detector: four independent routes -- gain at the corner, the -3 dB crossing, an external instrument measuring the same quantity, and an A/B by ear.

entries.name: KRZ_4POLE_F0_TO_3DB
entries.convention: converts the machine's f0 label to the -3 dB corner
